title: Rainfall-associated expansion of frog active communities is more boundary-biased than uniform activation predicts
frozen_core_claims: Recent-rain conditions are associated with expansion of the behaviourally realized acoustic community across active spatial footprint, local alpha richness and route gamma richness in NAAMP.
Active-unit taxonomic depth has the same recent-rain direction in the aligned NAAMP and FrogID analyses; this is cross-dataset consistency, not independent validation or a pooled effect-size claim.
The North American four-component incidence allocation strongly rejects the original magnitude-matched uniform-activation null under kappa 1, 2 and 5.
The allocation also strongly rejects a separately frozen persistence-preserving uniform-activation stress test at dry-state anchor weights 0.50, 0.75 and 0.90.

Under the primary persistence-preserving anchor a=0.75, boundary crossing is 92.0 percent observed versus 77.9 percent expected with a 73.4-82.8 percent 95 percent null interval; within-core rearrangement is 8.0 percent observed versus 22.1 percent expected.

Pairwise Sorensen change is small and lies within a post hoc +/-0.025 practical bound, but this is secondary context because the margin was selected after the conventional coefficient was known and the observed Sorensen slope lies inside the uniform-activation null distribution.
frozen_interpretation: Rainfall-associated expansion enters the behaviourally realized frog community more strongly across spatial and taxonomic boundaries than uniform activation predicts, and this departure survives a null that strongly preserves pair-specific dry species x stop identity.
frozen_negative_boundaries: No independent-validation or independent-replication claim for FrogID.
No worldwide or universal rainfall-response claim.
No pooled North America-Australia effect size and no equality-of-effect-size claim.
No claim that FrogID replicates the fixed ten-stop species x stop geometry.
No claim of identical mechanism across datasets or continents.
No rainfall causality, occupancy, abundance, colonization, extinction or demographic-recruitment claim.
No claim that temporary wetlands or heterogeneous activation thresholds are identified mechanisms.
Activation geometry remains falsified as a rainfall-specific species trait.
No title-level homogenization claim and no claim of confirmatory Sorensen equivalence.
